items.claim: For every real z≤0, exp(z)≤1+z+z²/2, with equality at z=0.
items.argument: Let g(t)=1+t−exp(t); monotonicity of exp gives g′(t)≥0 for t≤0. The mean value theorem makes g nondecreasing, hence g(t)≤g(0)=0 there. For f(t)=1+t+t²/2−exp(t), f′=g, so the mean value theorem gives f(z)≥f(0)=0. This proves the needed inequality without an imported Taylor remainder.

items.claim: For finite arms and horizon, pre-action reward vectors x_t∈[0,1]^k and strictly positive P_t∈Δ_k determine the draw A_t; only X_t=x_{t,A_t} is observed. With Y_t=1−X_t, set Yhat_{t,i}=1{A_t=i}Y_t/P_{t,i} and Xhat_{t,i}=1−Yhat_{t,i}.
items.argument: The definition fixes the choice-before-feedback timing and the loss-based estimator. Finite horizon, finite arms, bounded rewards, and positive probabilities make each observed estimate finite. Fixed sequences are oblivious; past-history choices are non-anticipating and chosen before A_t.

items.claim: At each pre-action history, for loss y_{t,i} and p=P_{t,i}>0, E[Yhat_{t,i}|F_{t−1}]=y_{t,i}, E[Yhat²_{t,i}|F_{t−1}]=y²_{t,i}/p, and Var(Yhat_{t,i}|F_{t−1})=y²_{t,i}(1−p)/p.
items.argument: Condition on a history atom. The estimate is y/p with probability p and 0 otherwise. Direct finite conditional sums give the first and second moments; centering the two values gives the variance. Finite histories avoid an unproved conditional-expectation pull-out step.

items.claim: Exp3 initializes cumulative estimated rewards at zero, samples from normalized exp(η times cumulative estimates), observes only the played reward, forms Xhat_{t,i}=1−1{A_t=i}(1−X_t)/P_{t,i}, and accumulates these estimates.
items.argument: Inductively the cumulative estimates remain finite. Each exponential weight is positive and finite, so the finite sum in the denominator is positive and finite; hence every action probability is strictly positive and the next observed estimate and update are finite.

items.claim: For an oblivious sequence x_t∈[0,1]^k, η=√(2 log(k)/(nk)) gives expected fixed-arm regret at most √(2nk log k). For deterministic pre-action past-adaptive rewards, the separately stated comparator is max_i E[Σ_t(x_{t,i}−X_t)], with the maximum outside expectation.
items.argument: Apply the local inequality exp(z)≤1+z+z²/2 to the nonpositive estimated-loss terms in the exponential-weight ratio, then telescope the potential against each fixed arm. Conditional moments bound the expected weighted squared loss by k per round. Conditional unbiasedness and the pathwise identity Σ_i P_{t,i}Xhat_{t,i}=X_t identify the expected arm gap. Tuning η balances log(k)/η with ηnk/2. No bounded-loss Hedge regret theorem is used.
